newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: CEO says CS Group has critical mass.
newsitem.headline: CEO says CS Group has critical mass.

text.p: CS Group's new chief executive Lukas Muehlemann said the reorganised company had critical mass in all its businesses and was under no pressure to acquire or sell off activities.

In an interview with the Swiss newspaper Basler Zeitung, Muehlemann said his main priority was implementing the new strategy of streamlining the group's business in four divisions created at the start of this year, when he took office.
Asked about stock market rumours that he would make big changes at CS Group as he had when he started as CEO of Swiss Reinsurance in 1994, Muehlemann said the two companies were very different.
"At the Credit Suisse Group, on the other hand, we have a very workable platform, critical mass everywhere and the prerequisites with the new structure for long-term success," he said.
"Of course I cannot fully rule out the possibility that we will take advantage of opportunities if they arise," he said.
"But I do not see any need for action based on the current structure," he added.

Muehlemann said Swiss Re, in contrast, had been divided when he arrived between a well-positioned reinsurance side and a less well-placed direct insurance business, which he then sold off to raise capital for expanding reinsurance.
Muehlemann declined to comment directly on another batch of recent market rumours that CS Group planned a closer alliance or merger of some kind with Swiss Re or Swiss insurer Winterthur.

CS Group has some product and marketing cooperation deals with Swiss Re and Winterthur. Speculation of farther-reaching plans has been fuelled by the fact that Muehlemann came from Swiss Re and was a colleague of the new Winterthur CEO, Thomas Wellauer, when both were still at McKinsey & Co in Zurich.
"It is better if we do not comment on the rumours," Muehlemann said.
"There are apparently no more limits to imagination these days," he added.
Muehlemann said each of the four business units was well positioned.
"In Swiss private and corporate retail business, where we are the largest provider alongside UBS with a market share of around 20 percent, I think we quite clearly have the necessary size," he said.
Credit Suisse's private banking unit was among the world's biggest, he added.

"In institutional asset management, our volume of $170 billion also gives us a basis for playing in the first league and Credit Suisse First Boston can count itself among the biggest global competitors with its profits last year of over five billion dollars," Muehlemann said.
Muehlemann said there would continue to be consolidation in the global investment banking business as smaller banks tried to move up to the top of the league.
"But we feel we are in a good starting position," he added.
